incidente.resumo: A fire at a Telstra exchange in Chatswood, Sydney, was contained but damaged some power infrastructure, and a number of customers lost mobile and fixed services; Telstra also reported a related issue impacting SMS messaging, with messages held while it was resolved. Jetstar delayed at least nine flights and moved some check-in to manual. The text, written during the incident, does not say how service was restored.

descricao.texto: A fire at a Telstra exchange in Chatswood was contained but damaged some of the power infrastructure; according to a Telstra spokesperson, as a result a number of customers were experiencing loss of service.
trechos: A fire at a Telstra exchange in Chatswood, in Sydney’s north, has disrupted communications across the city and forced Jetstar to delay several flights
A Telstra spokesperson told Business Insider that fire was contained but had damaged some of the power infrastructure.
“As a result a number customers are experiencing loss of service.

perguntas_em_aberto: Telstra technicians were completing a full assessment of the impact of the fire.
Telstra was investigating a related issue impacting SMS messaging.

observacoes: The article was written during the incident and quotes Telstra tweets dated February 2, 2017. It does not describe SMS messages being sent to random destinations or corrupted; it only says Telstra was investigating a related SMS issue and holding messages. AussieOutages.com reported problems in several state capitals, which the article says appear to be more widespread. Jetstar reported 9 flights delayed about 45 minutes.
